title: POC weekly sync - NexaHealth onboarding
summary: Weekly POC sync for NexaHealth. Reviewed initial benchmark results (latency/cost tradeoffs), confirmed infra access needs (VPC peering, service account keys, SSO metadata), discussed model variant and quantization options for inference, and agreed on next steps: security docs, end-to-end perf run, and updated timeline.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-06-16 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Ava Chen (Redwood AE), Marco Ortiz (Redwood SE), Dr. Priya Patel (NexaHealth), Samir Rao (NexaHealth), Lena Kim (NexaHealth)

Auto-summary (auto): quick sync on onboarding; some noisy audio at start

00:00 Ava Chen: ok good afternoon everyone thanks for joining, uh we'll do a quick 45 min sync, agenda is access, bench results, and next steps. Marco and I will run through the perf numbers then hand it over to Priya for questions.
00:18 Marco Ortiz: hey all, quick note - i ran the first end-to-end with the quantized variant last night, so we'll show that. the test was on 8k context on Redwood-dedicated pool, turned on prefix cache. performance numbers might look noisy since the dataset is small.
00:37 Dr. Priya Patel: thanks, Marco. quick housekeeping: we still need VPC peering details, and Samir is on for infra questions. also want to make sure SSO works for our product team.
00:50 Samir Rao: yeah we got your SSH key ping but haven't done the peering yet, we need the peering CIDRs and the acceptance window.
01:05 Ava Chen: noted - Marco will share the exact CIDRs and the runbook. Marco, did you capture the CIDR range for the dedicated pool?
01:16 Marco Ortiz: yep, i'll put that in the runbook. currently the pool sits in 10.41.0.0/16 for the demo cluster, production will be 10.128/9 - sorry, i missed a digit there, it's 10.128.0.0/9. i'll confirm in the doc.
01:32 Dr. Priya Patel: there's sometimes confusion with the prefixes, i've seen that, so thanks for confirming.
01:45 Lena Kim: on the sample dataset: we plan to share anonymized query logs and 1k sample records, that's ready by end of week. is 1k sufficient for the perf run?
01:56 Marco Ortiz: 1k is fine but please include the long-tail examples - the ones with multi-turn context and long system prompts. that stresses KV cache and batching behavior.
02:12 Ava Chen: priya, also for success criteria, we had the SLA targets as < 150ms p50 for single-turn LLM calls and p95 under 350ms for short prompts. is that still accurate?
02:25 Dr. Priya Patel: p50 < 200ms is fine, we can relax p50 a bit, but p95 we want tighter, maybe 300ms. cost is also a factor - want to see tokens per second and billable units.
02:40 Marco Ortiz: noted. in the initial run we saw p50 ~190ms and p95 ~420ms for the non-quantized variant, with quantized BF16 we saw p95 drop to ~320ms. there's a tradeoff in quality vs quantization.
03:02 Samir Rao: can you speak to how KV cache warm-up affects those p95 numbers? we saw a lot of variance on first call.
03:15 Marco Ortiz: yes first-call overhead is higher. with prefix caching enabled and warm-up traffic it's much better. the plan is to run a warm-up script that seeds the cache with the most common prefixes. i'll add that to the runbook.
03:34 Lena Kim: related question - what's the deployment model you'd recommend for us? we want predictable latency but also lower cost for off-peak. dedicated pool plus autoscale or private VPC?
03:47 Ava Chen: typically for NexaHealth we recommend Dedicated for predictable throughput and data isolation; you can enable autoscaling policies with a reserved baseline and burst capacity. Private (VPC) is suggested if you need an on-prem connector or airgap, but that adds ops overhead.
04:06 Dr. Priya Patel: for compliance we need KMS integration and audit logs retention 3 years ideally. does Redwood support customer-managed KMS and longer audit retention?
04:18 Marco Ortiz: yes, we support customer-managed KMS for Private deployments. For hosted/dedicated we can integrate with your KMS in VPC mode; audit log retention is configurable as an add-on. i'll surface the SOC2 and retention options in the security note.
04:35 Samir Rao: can you also share the SSO metadata? our security team needs SAML metadata for the dev/test tenant.
04:45 Ava Chen: yes we'll send SAML metadata and a brief SSO walkthrough.
04:52 Marco Ortiz: quick note on model variants - we tested two: redwood-turbo-1 (non-quantized baseline) and redwood-lite-q3 (quantized). in conversation quality evals, the team saw negligible delta on the clinical QA prompts but there were hallucination cases on the summarization task with the quantized model.
05:15 Dr. Priya Patel: that's important - for notes summarization we need conservative outputs. are there knobs to reduce hallucination while staying quantized?
05:25 Marco Ortiz: yes, we can tune sampling temperature, use higher nucleus (top_p) thresholds, and enforce reranking/verification steps. also running an evalharness with your test set will give concrete metrics.
05:38 Lena Kim: can Redwood run the eval and provide a short report comparing recall/precision/hallucination rates?
05:45 Marco Ortiz: absolutely, we can run the eval, but we need the labeled ground truth and the exact prompts you use. Priya, can you share those?
05:57 Dr. Priya Patel: yes i'll share a 200-record labeled slice and the prompts.
06:06 Ava Chen: great. timeline check: if we get sample data by 2027-06-20 and run warm-up and perf on 2027-06-21, we could have a draft report early next week. does that align?
06:20 Samir Rao: yes, that window works but we need a 2-hr peering maintenance window; i'll propose one on the 18th after 10pm UTC.
06:32 Marco Ortiz: that works, i'll make the runbook tolerant of brief downtime but recommend the perf run post-peering.
06:44 Dr. Priya Patel: also procurement flagged potential vendor review. do you have SOC2 docs and a data processing addendum we can share with legal?
06:56 Ava Chen: yes - i'll attach SOC2 type II excerpts and the DPA; expect in the email later today.
07:06 Lena Kim: pricing ask - can you give an estimate for the pilot (3 months, expected 2M tokens/month) and an estimate with and without dedicated baseline?
07:20 Ava Chen: i'll have pricing in the next email; high-level: hosted usage-only would be pay-as-you-go, Dedicated baseline gives unit discounts. i'll include an illustrative cost sheet.
07:33 Marco Ortiz: one more technical: do you want us to run the perf on your dev data inside your VPC or use a synthetic mirror on Redwood? the dev data path gives more accurate I/O characteristics.
07:47 Samir Rao: we'd prefer in-VPC to avoid data egress and to be realistic. we can set up a dev subnet and accept the peering.
07:58 Ava Chen: ok we'll proceed with in-VPC perf. Marco will send runbook and CIDRs.
08:06 Marco Ortiz: i'll also include the warm-up script and suggested warm-up traffic pattern.
08:18 Dr. Priya Patel: last thing - can you include a quick note on how cache invalidation interacts with model rollouts? we have frequent model updates in our infra.
08:30 Marco Ortiz: short answer: cache keys are tied to model version and prompt fingerprint; when you roll models, you can either invalidate cache per model or maintain cross-model compatibility by pinning tokenization. we'll add a section on safe rollout.
08:45 Ava Chen: perfect. recap of action items: Marco send runbook + CIDRs + warm-up script; Ava send SAML + SOC2 + pricing sheet; Priya share 1k sample + 200 labeled slice + prompts; Samir propose peering window; Lena confirm KPIs. we'll meet after perf run for the results review.
09:08 Dr. Priya Patel: that sounds good, thanks all.
09:14 Ava Chen: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with links to docs and timeline.

References shared: runbook link (placeholder) https://redwood.link/runbook-nexa, security excerpt (placeholder) https://redwood.link/soc2-nexa, pricing spreadsheet (placeholder) https://redwood.link/price-nexa
